reasons: The same Docker reproducer triggered a sanitizer or race report only after introduction.

The deterministic fast-path run (default command, no setpref) produced identical non-crashing exit=3 on all three revisions because Atomics.waitAsync is gated behind the javascript.options.atomics_wait_async pref (default false in this build) and the PoC never got past 'Atomics.waitAsync is not a function' — inconclusive, not evidence of absence. Adapting the command to add --setpref=atomics_wait_async=true (required to reach the affected code at all) reproduces the crash cleanly and reversibly: pre_intro and post_benign run the identical PoC and command to completion with exit=0; post_intro crashes deterministically under ASAN with a SEGV inside the exact function named in meta.json's root cause (atomics_notify_impl's same-thread fast path resolving a cross-realm/cross-compartment Promise without entering its realm first), via the same call stack the original reporter captured. This confirms the intro commit introduces the regression and the benign-companion/fix removes it, using one invariant reproducer across all three builds.

agent_oracle.description: JS shell PoC (reporter's testcase from bug 2013562, copied verbatim as /poc/poc.js): creates a second compartment via newGlobal({newCompartment:true}), shares a SharedArrayBuffer-backed Int32Array with it, calls Atomics.waitAsync(ta,0,0,5000) 10x in the main compartment (registering same-thread async waiters whose Promise lives in the main compartment's realm), then calls Atomics.notify(ta2,0) from JS evaluated in the OTHER compartment. Run with: `/work/obj-verify-js/dist/bin/js --fuzzing-safe --no-threads --setpref=atomics_wait_async=true $INPUT` (the --setpref is required because javascript.options.atomics_wait_async defaults to false in this build; the deterministic fast-path run without it never reaches Atomics.waitAsync, explaining the earlier non-crashing exit=3 'Atomics.waitAsync is not a function' result).
agent_oracle.target_evidence:
post_intro (3b5eb00effeb): exit=134, AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x0 (WRITE), in MOZ_CrashSequence/MOZ_Crash -> js::ContextChecks::fail -> JSContext::check -> js::ResolvePromiseInternal (Promise.cpp) -> PromiseObject::resolve -> js::atomics_notify_impl (AtomicsObject.cpp:1454) -> atomics_notify. This is the same-thread fast path in atomics_notify_impl resolving a waitAsync Promise while JSContext::realm()/compartment differs from the promise's compartment (compartment-mismatch assertion firing as a null-deref SEGV under ASAN), exactly matching meta.json's root_cause and the reporter's own backtrace (candidate_01_c001_crash_data.txt) through the identical call chain (atomics_notify_impl -> PromiseObject::resolve -> ResolvePromiseInternal -> ContextChecks::check -> fail).
pre_intro (85ed04eda9d2): same command/input, exit=0, no crash, no sanitizer report.
post_benign (fix-paired companion): same command/input, exit=0, no crash, no sanitizer report — matching the 'Enter correct realm before resolving same-thread waitAsync promise' fix message.
